intro: Schiaparelli — Europe's second Mars landing attempt — separated from ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter on October 16, 2016, then crashed into Meridiani Planum at ~540 km/h three days later. A software glitch caused the parachute and braking thrusters to disengage 50 seconds early, while the lander was still 3.7 km above the surface. The wreckage was spotted by MRO HiRISE within a week. Lessons learned shaped the ExoMars Rosalind Franklin rover, now slated for 2028 launch.
